content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Honolulu

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires a combination of formal education and project-management experience. Review PMI's specific hour and credential thresholds for your background—high-school diploma, associate degree, or bachelor's degree each carry different experience requirements. Gather documentation of your project work to verify you meet the baseline.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP Bootcamp. Our courses run nationwide and are designed for working professionals in Honolulu's tourism, healthcare, military, construction, government, and renewable-energy sectors. Complete all required contact hours before you can submit your PMI application.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After finishing the 35-hour course, create your PMI account and complete the formal credential application. You'll verify your education and experience hours, agree to PMI's Code of Conduct, and pay the examination fee. Allow time for PMI to review and approve your application before scheduling your exam.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—study guides, practice questions, and instructor support—to solidify your knowledge. Once approved, schedule your exam at a Pearson VUE testing center. The PMP® is a computer-based, proctored exam; you may test at a center or at home, depending on your preference.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP® Credential
steps_items.text: After passing, your PMP® is valid for three years. During each renewal cycle, earn Professional Development Units (PDUs) through continuing education, volunteer work, and knowledge sharing. Submit your renewal application and fee before expiration to keep your credential active and current in your career.
